entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv17879"/><div sID="gen36438" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv17879"/>3. The Greek aorist tense implies, "For ye have died once for all" (<reference osisRef="Col.2.12">Col 2:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.6.4-Rom.6.7">Ro 6:4-7</reference>). It is not said, Ye must die practically to the world in order to become dead with Christ; but the latter is assumed as once for all having taken place in the regeneration; what believers are told is, Develop this spiritual life in practice. "No one longs for eternal, incorruptible, and immortal life, unless he be wearied of this temporal, corruptible, and mortal life" [Augustine].<div eID="gen36438" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen36439" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and your life ... hid--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ps.83.3">Psa 83:3</reference>); like a seed buried in the earth; compare "planted," <reference osisRef="Rom.6.5">Ro 6:5</reference>. Compare <reference osisRef="Matt.13.31">Mt 13:31</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.13.33">33</reference>, "like ... leaven ... hid." As the glory of Christ now is hid from the world, so also the glory of believers' inner life, proceeding from communion with Him, is still hidden with Christ in God; but (<reference osisRef="Col.3.4">Col 3:4</reference>) when Christ, the Source of this life, shall manifest Himself in glory, then shall their hidden glory be manifest, and correspond in appearance to its original [Neander]. The Christian's secret communion with God will now at times make itself seen without his intending it (<reference osisRef="Matt.5.14">Mt 5:14</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.5.16">16</reference>); but his full manifestation is at Christ's manifestation (<reference osisRef="Matt.13.43">Mt 13:43</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.8.19-Rom.8.23">Ro 8:19-23</reference>). "It doth not yet appear (Greek, 'is not yet manifested') what we shall be" (<reference osisRef="1John.3.2">1Jo 3:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Pet.1.7">1Pe 1:7</reference>). As yet Christians do not always recognize the "life" of one another, so hidden is it, and even at times doubt as to their own life, so weak is it, and so harassed with temptations (<reference osisRef="Ps.51.1-Ps.51.19">Psa 51:1-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.7.1-Rom.7.25">Ro 7:1-25</reference>).<div eID="gen36439" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen36440" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in God--</hi>to whom Christ has ascended. Our "life" is "laid up for" us in God (<reference osisRef="Col.1.5">Col 1:5</reference>), and is secured by the decree of Him who is invisible to the world (<reference osisRef="2Tim.4.8">2Ti 4:8</reference>). <div eID="gen36440" type="x-p"/>

Translate, "When Christ shall be manifested who is our life (<reference osisRef="John.11.25">Joh 11:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.14.6">14:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="John.14.19">19</reference>), then shall ye also with Him be manifested in glory" (<reference osisRef="1Pet.4.13">1Pe 4:13</reference>). "The peace of God." Therefore Christ is God. Peace was His legacy to His disciples before He left them (<reference osisRef="John.14.27">Joh 14:27</reference>), "My peace I give unto you." Peace is peculiarly His to give. Peace follows love (<reference osisRef="Col.3.14">Col 3:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.4.2">Ep 4:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Eph.4.3">3</reference>).<div eID="gen36482" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen36483" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">rule--</hi>literally, "sit as umpire"; the same Greek verb simple, as appears compounded (<reference osisRef="Col.2.18">Col 2:18</reference>).
